# parity-fuzz --mode redir baseline: normalized signatures of KNOWN gaps.
# A divergence whose signature is here is allowed; a NEW one fails CI.
# Regenerate: parity-fuzz --mode redir --count N --verify 3  (copy NEW-signature lines).
#
# No known gaps — 4000 cases run clean. Covers redirections, MULTIOS (zsh tees a
# duplicated fd rather than overwriting), fd juggling (`exec {fd}>`, `>&-`),
# here-strings, append-vs-truncate, stdout/stderr ordering, and function-level
# redirections (`f() { … } > file`).
#
# The mode had a clean baseline from the start but was NOT gated in CI until the
# function-redirect arms were added. Gating it is what makes the baseline mean
# anything.
#
# ONE CONFIRMED BUG IS NOT GENERATED HERE — the same-fd merge case:
#
#     f() { print -r -- body } > f1; f > f2
#         zsh    f1=[body] f2=[body]
#         zshrs  f1=[body] f2=[]
#
# A function's redirections are not applied at definition time: C stores them on
# the shfunc (`shf->redir`, c:Src/exec.c:5397) and re-opens them on every call.
# What zshrs gets wrong is how they COMBINE with a redirection at the CALL site
# (c:Src/exec.c:3565-3578):
#
#     redir2 = ecgetredirs(&s);        /* the DEFINITION's */
#     if (!redir) redir = redir2;
#     else while (nonempty(redir2))
#              addlinknode(redir, ugetnode(redir2));
#
# The call's redirections come first and the definition's are APPENDED to the
# SAME list. One flat list is what lets MULTIOS tee across both. zshrs has no
# per-function redir storage — compile_zsh.rs (`Redirected(FuncDef(...))`) wraps
# the BODY in `Redirected(Cursh(body), redirs)` instead, so the def-redirs and
# the call-redirs apply as NESTED scopes; the inner (def) scope owns the fd and
# the outer (call) redirect silently receives nothing. `unsetopt multios` agrees
# on both shells, which is what pins the cause to the merge rather than to the
# redirect itself.
#
# This is a real bug, not cosmetic: output goes to the wrong file with no error.
# Fixing it faithfully needs substrate that does not exist yet — the def-redirs
# must be available AT THE CALL so both join one MULTIOS list, which means
# per-function redir storage plus a call-time merge inside the
# WithRedirectsBegin/End machinery. The redirect scope is currently opened by
# the COMPILER at the call site, before CallFunction runs. Left unfixed rather
# than half-fixed.
#
# It is EXCLUDED from the vocabulary rather than baselined because signature()
# keys a baseline entry off the LAST line of the program, and gen_redir's
# cleanup statement (`cd /; command rm -rf $d`) can end up there after
# minimization — an entry that would allow ANY redir divergence through. The
# `errdef` form keeps def+call coverage on DIFFERENT fds (2> on the definition,
# > at the call), which does not hit the merge and passes. Add the merge form
# back once the call-time merge exists.
#
# The function-redirect arms tag their final statement (`defonly`, `callonly`,
# `recall`, `errdef`) precisely so each form signs distinctly; a shared readback
# line would collapse them onto one signature, and baselining the failing one
# would then mask the passing ones.
#
# NOCLOBBER / `>|` / `<>` / multiple-INPUT MULTIOS (verified-correct coverage):
# the mode gated multiple-OUTPUT tee but not the clobber-control and read-side
# forms. A dedicated arm now exercises `>` over an existing file under
# NO_CLOBBER (errors "file exists", rc=1, target untouched — c:exec.c:4269), the
# `>|` clobber override (c:4256), `<>` read-write (c:4310 O_RDWR), and two `<`
# concatenating their inputs under MULTIOS. Each embeds a distinct tag
# (`NOCLOB`/`CLOBBER`/`RDWR`/`MULTIIN`) for signature separation. All
# hand-verified equal on both shells.
#
# Any divergence here is a regression.
